faq.answer: No. Trust is an expectation tendency, not moral character.
faq.question: Does strong Trust make someone a good person?

faq.answer: Yes. Closeness can grow through evidence, time, boundaries, and repair.
faq.question: Can someone with weaker Trust build close relationships?

faq.answer: No. Strong Trust can be informed, and caution can be miscalibrated. Judge evidence directly.
faq.question: Is Trust the same as ignorance or immaturity?

faq.answer: Sometimes, through safety, accountability, consistent behavior, and choice. This page cannot prescribe or guarantee repair.
faq.question: Can Trust be rebuilt after fraud or betrayal?

faq.answer: Norms and institutions can shape expression, but this package provides no individual cultural correction.
faq.question: Does culture affect Trust?

sections.body:
Trust concerns the initial expectation that other people are generally honest and well-intentioned. It is not morality, gullibility, certainty, a safety assessment, or proof that one specific person deserves access.

“Trust within Agreeableness: expectations about others’ intentions” is used on this page as a descriptive construct within the NEO/IPIP-NEO 30-facet framework. The official IPIP resource describes scales that measure constructs similar to NEO facets and lists item mappings ([S11](https://ipip.ori.org/Finding_Scales_to_Measure_Particular_Constructs.htm)); this does not make scores from different instruments, translations, or products interchangeable.

FermatMind has not published product-level reliability, validity, Chinese norms, or individual predictive evidence for the score discussed on this page. This material is for self-observation and education. It is not for clinical diagnosis, hiring screening, school admission, or replacing a career decision.

> **Content method and update:** FermatMind Editorial prepared this page with AI-assisted drafting and checked terminology, boundaries, and evidence against public personality-psychology sources. It is for self-understanding and education; it is not clinical diagnosis, hiring screening, or individual-outcome prediction. Substantive update: 2026-07-19; review mode: solo_operator; not clinically reviewed.
sections.heading: Evidence and Interpretation Boundaries

sections.body: A stronger tendency begins with more benign expectations; a weaker tendency begins with more caution or suspicion. Healthy decisions still require evidence, boundaries, stakes, and verification. Experience can shape behavior without fully defining a general tendency.
sections.heading: Precise Definition

sections.body: Trust belongs to [Agreeableness](/en/personality/big-five/agreeableness), reflecting how readily cooperative intent is attributed to others.
sections.heading: Parent Domain

sections.body:
- **Trust versus Warmth:** Warmth concerns friendly expression; Trust concerns expectations of intent.
- **Trust versus Straightforwardness:** [Straightforwardness](/en/personality/big-five/facets/straightforwardness) concerns one’s own communication strategy.
- **Trust versus verified reliability:** Direct history and safeguards should guide consequential reliance.
sections.heading: Distinguishing Neighboring Facets

sections.body: Stronger Trust may appear as sharing responsibility early, interpreting ambiguity benignly, or accepting statements provisionally. Weaker Trust may appear as checking, limiting access, reading incentives, or requiring history. Fraud exposure, discrimination, trauma, role, and power can alter visible behavior.
sections.heading: Behavioral Cues

sections.body: Someone may trust friends but verify vendors, or be cautious online and open in a local community. Higher stakes justify more checking at any trait level. A protective response after betrayal is not reducible to a personality label.
sections.heading: Contextual Differences

sections.body:
- Assuming good faith at first contact.
- Delegating with limited monitoring.
- Repairing misunderstandings through dialogue.
- Missing manipulation cues when verification is absent.
- Feeling personally hurt when trust is violated.
sections.heading: Possible Expressions When Stronger

sections.body:
- Seeking evidence before reliance.
- Separating politeness from access.
- Detecting incentives and inconsistencies.
- Withholding cooperation after adequate evidence appears.
- Making closeness develop slowly but deliberately.
sections.heading: Possible Expressions When Weaker

sections.body: Stronger Trust can lower coordination friction and make cooperation easier. Possible costs include exploitation or delayed detection of harm. Weaker Trust can support risk control; possible costs include guarded relationships and excessive monitoring. Neither level establishes goodness or intelligence.
sections.heading: Strengths and Costs

sections.body: A founder gives a new contractor limited access, clear milestones, and respectful autonomy. Trust is paired with verification rather than treated as all-or-nothing.
sections.heading: An Original Case

sections.body: A person cautious after fraud builds a close relationship gradually through consistent behavior and explicit boundaries. Lower initial Trust does not prevent intimacy.
sections.heading: An Original Counterexample

sections.body:
1. What is your default interpretation of ambiguous intent?
2. Which stakes trigger verification?
3. Does evidence revise suspicion and confidence symmetrically?
4. What access can be granted in stages?
5. When does caution protect you, and when does it block cooperation?
sections.heading: Self-Observation Questions

sections.body: Choose one low-stakes collaboration and define a small reversible trust step plus a verification point. Observe whether expectations update with evidence. Do not use this exercise where safety is uncertain.
sections.heading: Low-Risk Action Experiment

sections.body: Return to [Agreeableness](/en/personality/big-five/agreeableness) or the [30-facet guide](/en/personality/big-five/facets). Continue with [Straightforwardness](/en/personality/big-five/facets/straightforwardness), [Altruism](/en/personality/big-five/facets/altruism), [Compliance](/en/personality/big-five/facets/compliance), [Modesty](/en/personality/big-five/facets/modesty), [Tender-Mindedness](/en/personality/big-five/facets/tender-mindedness).
